Q: Is it bad practice to programmatically add submodules to sys? A:

Yes that is true. But in Python, this boundaries are a bit different. Python classes are first-class objects and naturally act as namespaces. Despite this, using a bare class just to group things is often called a namespace class.

Q: How can I work with the USB DFU bootloader without using the VBUS and ID lines for STM32F4xx? A:

Use the built-in DFU

Many of the ST ARM chips have a DFU utility built in. To use it, you need to raise BOOT0 and plug it in. Full documentation is available from ST, in AN3156. The code is currently here although it might move from time to time. Look for DFUSE on the ST site. There is a video on YouTube.

Using VBUS for normal USB

  1. USB either compiles for or without VBUS signaling, depending on a flag set in STM32CubeMX.

  2. ST provides all the necessary documentation and software concerning DFU and USB on their product pages. They also provide a working DFU. You need to raise BOOT0 and possibly BOOT1, depending on the device you have.

  3. You can write your own DFU; its not magic. All it does is look for a specific file name on USB and write the contents to non-volatile memory.

Go through the bootloader code you have (or STs) and see how they trigger if you want specific operation, for example, live update of a working device.

It is possible to have multiple copies of firmware loaded in flash, and then choose which one to run either by setting pins, or by writing to the boot address

Q: Salesforce error=redirect_uri_mismatch&error_description=redirect_uri A:

If you are getting error of mísmatch ủri then strong text Go to Salesforce page and go to the connected app Go to Setup (gear icon in the top right). In the Quick Find box, search for "App Manager" and select it. Find your connected app in the list and click on "Edit" next to it. Scroll down to the "Web App Settings" section. In the "Callback URL" field, enter your new redirect URI. If you have multiple redirect URIs, you can add them by clicking the "Add" button next to the Callback URL field. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click "Save".

Q: How to edit the merge-commit message with Egit? A:

You can change the merge commit in both the History and Git Staging view after you created the merge commit.

The History view

You can right-click the commit in the History view and choose Modify > Reword:

This opens a window for rewording the commit message:

This will recreate the merge commit with the new name. If there are additional commits depending on it in the current branch, these would be recreated as well.

When you are doing this with the most recent (HEAD) commit, this is equivalent to an "amend" operation. When you are doing this on previous commits, this is more or less an "interactive rebase" (as suggested by the title). If you don't fully understand what that is, I recommend not doing this in repositories you care about (basically it's fine if all affected commits are not pushed and/or you are the only person working on that project). Do not modify old commits unless you know exactly what you are doing.

The Git Staging view

Alternatively you can open the Git Staging view and click the Amend (Edit Previous Commit) button to modify the last commit (HEAD). This also allows changing some files.

Once that mode is enabled, it should show you the message of the merge commit on the right. You can change the commit message and use the "Commit" button to confirm it.

Warning

Please note that doing so will overwrite/rewrite the merge commit. While you can amend the commit when it isn't pushed anywhere, please don't do that after pushing the relevant commit.

If you do it nonetheless, you will have the same merge commit twice (locally and on the remote) with different commit messages (the histories "diverged") resulting in you not being able to push it unless you resolve it (a force push would overwrite the remote but anyone who already pulled the changes would get in the same painful situation afterwards so you shouldn't do that in any situations where others may depend on that branch).

Changing it for the future

If you think there should be an option for entering a custom message when merging, feel free to create a pull request at the EGit repository (but please make sure this doesn't degrade the workflow/add unnecessary steps for people that are happy with the default message). I'm sure they are happy about contributions.
